INFORMATION ABOUT STUDY

Title of Study: Decision-Making and Finger Agility

You are invited to participate in a research study. This study is being conducted by the Department of Social Psychology at Tilburg University. The intention of this study is to research and gain knowledge on how people make decisions. This study involves: 


	(i) two rounds of a decision-making scenario (where you could earn bonus payment)
	(ii) a task involving finger agility
	(iii) a questionnaire. 


This study will take approximately 18 minutes to complete. 

 

Participation, Benefits and Risks 

Participation in this research study is completely voluntary. You have the right to withdraw at any time or refuse to participate entirely without providing any explanation. If you desire to withdraw, please simply close your internet browser. There will be no negative consequences if you withdraw or refuse to participate. After participating in this research, you will be given a completion code with which you can collect your monetary reward ($1.80) for participating. Depending on the outcomes of the decisions you make, you may earn additional bonus payment. Risks are minimal for involvement in this study.

  

Requirement

To participate in this study, you need to be at least 18 years old. 

 

Confidentiality

All data obtained from participants will be kept anonymous. There will be no record that links the data collected from you with any personal data from which you could be identified (e.g., your name, address, email, etc.). Once anonymized, these data may be made available to researchers via accessible data repositories and possibly used for novel purposes. The data will be stored for at least 10 years. 

 

Questions

If you have questions regarding this study, you may contact the researcher How Hwee Ong at h.h.ong@tilburguniversity.edu.

 

This study has received approval from the Tilburg School of Behavioral Sciences’ Ethical Review Board. If you have any remarks or complaints regarding this research, you may also contact the Ethics Review Board of Tilburg School of Social and Behavioral Sciences via erb@tilburguniversity.edu.

FINGER AGILITY TASK

 

 
You will soon be asked to perform a finger agility task that tests your speed and reaction time.


	You can choose between two versions of this task (Version A and Version B). 
	Both versions require you to quickly move your mouse cursor and click your mouse repeatedly (or screen taps if you are using a device with touch screen). 
	The duration (time taken) of both versions is the same.  
	Previous participants have indicated that both versions are equally interesting.
	Some previous participants have indicated that Version B hurt their hand a little. Therefore, we want to provide the disclaimer to you that Version B could cause a small amount of hand pain.
	Any hand pain caused by Version B will be harmless as it will quickly dissipate when the task is over, with no long-lasting pain. 


Now, please choose which version of the task that you would like to perform?
